agentReply.interpretation: The driver of Vehicle A had 10.43 seconds of continuous line of sight to the semitrailer before impact, providing sufficient perception-reaction time.

prt.detail: The driver of Vehicle A: 2015 4-door passenger sedan had a continuous line of sight to Vehicle T (Semitrailer): 2003 53-ft white refrigerated van semitrailer for 10.43 s before impact (t=0.00–10.43 s), from the start of the reconstructed timeline, so this is a lower bound. Typical perception-reaction time is 1.5 s (range 1–2.5 s). Time available is more than the 2.5 s upper bound, so there was time to perceive and begin reacting. Vehicle T (Semitrailer): 2003 53-ft white refrigerated van semitrailer came within 3 m of the centerline of this driver's remaining path 1.73 s before impact. Kinematic estimate from the reconstructed geometry; it does not account for attention, conspicuity, glare or expectation.
